exposure: prelabour caesarean section at full term (39(0) -40(6) weeks)
prelabour caesarean section at early term (37(0) -38(6) weeks)
Timing of delivery (early term vs full term)
outcome: Neonatal Critical Care Unit (NCCU) admission with serious morbidity
cohort: 22,954 viable singleton births by prelabor cesarean section at term (37-40 weeks) at a single center in Australia between 1998 and 2013
finding: Infants born in the public hospital had more adverse outcomes and treatment escalations, despite early-term prelabor cesarean sections occurring more often in the private hospital.
mod_finding: Infants born to those in the public hospital cohort who underwent pre-labor cesarean had more adverse outcomes and treatment escalations than those in the private hospital cohort, despite early term prelabor cesareans occuring more often in the private hospital.
